resignationPay.title: Resignation Payout Calculator
resignationPay.subtitle: Pick your last working day to see severance pay, unused annual leave pay, unemployment benefits and the year-end tax settlement in one place.

in.lastHint: The last day you actually work. Your separation date is the next day; for unemployment benefits this day is the separation day.
in.payHint: Base pay plus monthly allowances before tax. If it varied, enter the 3-month average.
in.bonusHint: Total bonuses received in the last 12 months. 3/12 of it counts toward average wage.

leave.label: Unused annual leave
leave.available: You can use {days} days of leave on your last day (calculated from your start date).
leave.none: No annual leave has accrued by your last day.

in.dependentsHint: Family members eligible for the basic deduction, excluding you (income of 1 million KRW or less). Leave 0 if unsure.
in.disabled: I have a registered disability (same benefit days as age 50+)
in.invalid: Your last working day is before your start date. Please check the dates.

advised.label: Recommended resignation (company reasons)
advised.hint: The company asked you to leave for business reasons. Check that the separation certificate states this, not personal reasons.

contract.label: Fixed-term contract ended
contract.hint: Leaving at contract end qualifies for unemployment benefits. If the company offered a renewal and you declined, it may count as voluntary.

closure.label: Business closure or bankruptcy
closure.hint: Leaving because the company closed or went bankrupt qualifies for unemployment benefits.

dismissal.label: Dismissal
dismissal.hint: Dismissal qualifies for benefits, but not if dismissed for serious misconduct such as a prison sentence, major damage to the business or long unauthorized absence (Employment Insurance Act Art. 58).

voluntary.label: Voluntary (new job, personal reasons)
voluntary.hint: Leaving for your own reasons normally disqualifies you from benefits, unless there is a justified reason such as unpaid wages, harassment or a 3-hour round-trip commute.

total.label: Money you get when you leave (est.)
total.withUe: {sure} from the company + {ue} unemployment benefits (if you apply and qualify)
total.noUe: {sure} from the company. Unemployment benefits are excluded under these conditions.
total.payBy: Your final pay, severance and leave pay must be paid within 14 days of separation (by {date}) under Labor Standards Act Art. 36. The deadline can be extended only by agreement in special circumstances.

sev.title: Severance pay
sev.irp: Moved to an IRP and taken as a pension, the tax drops to {tax} (30% off for the first 10 years of payouts).
sev.none: No severance pay because you have worked less than a year. Work until {date} ({days} more days) to qualify.

leave.title: Unused leave pay
leave.note: Calculated as monthly pay ÷ 209 hours × 8 hours. If your pay includes allowances that change monthly, the actual ordinary wage may be lower. Leave pay is employment income, so it is included in the tax settlement below.

ue.title: Unemployment benefits
ue.voluntary: Voluntary resignation is normally not eligible (Employment Insurance Act Art. 58). With a recognized justified reason you could receive the amount below ({total}).
ue.short: Counting only this job, your insured days are about {unit}, short of {min}. You may still qualify if insured days at other employers within 18 months before leaving bring the total to {min} or more.

applied.cap: 60% of your average wage exceeds the cap for {year} separations, so the cap of {cap} applies.
applied.floor: The {year} minimum of {floor} (minimum wage × 80% × 8 hours) applies.

ue.applyUntil: Benefits must be received within 12 months from the day after you leave (by {date}), so apply right away.

tax.title: Year-end tax settlement on leaving
tax.note: On resignation the company settles with only basic deductions and the standard tax credit. Withholding is estimated from the simplified tax table assuming all pay is taxable. Card, medical and pension savings deductions can be claimed in the May {year} income tax return.

share.label: Money I get if I leave on {last}
share.subNoUe: Severance, leave pay and tax settlement
share.text: If I leave on {last}, I get {total}.

sim.title: Try another last day
sim.desc: A few days can decide whether severance or new leave accrues, and the year you leave changes unemployment benefit limits.
sim.note: Totals add severance, leave pay and unemployment benefits (when eligible) only. Salary for the extra days and the tax settlement are excluded, and new leave is assumed unused.
sim.ueYear: Leaving in {year} changes the daily benefit to {daily} (based on that year's minimum wage and cap).

todo.title: What to do after you leave

pay.title: Check final payments by {date}
pay.desc: Make sure your final pay, severance and leave pay arrived, and that you received withholding receipts for employment and retirement income. If they are still unpaid after the deadline, you can file a wage complaint with the Ministry of Employment and Labor (call 1350).

ue.title: Check the separation certificate, then apply on Work24
ue.desc: Confirm the company filed your insurance loss report and separation certificate, then register as a job seeker and apply for benefits on Work24 from {from}. After {until} you lose any remaining days.

health.title: Compare health insurance continuation
health.desc: The day after you leave you become a regional subscriber. If the regional premium is higher, you can apply to keep paying your employee premium (at least 1 year as an employee subscriber, apply within 2 months of the first regional premium due date, up to 36 months).

irp.title: Receive severance into an IRP
irp.desc: Severance is generally paid into your own IRP account (exceptions such as leaving at 55 or older). Tax is deferred while it stays in the IRP and cut by 30–50% if taken as a pension. Open an account before you leave and tell the company.

may.title: File income tax in May {year}
may.desc: If you did not take a new job that year, file your income tax return on Hometax in May to claim card, medical and pension savings deductions left out at resignation. If you were rehired that year, give your new employer the previous withholding receipt for its year-end settlement.

exceptions.title: When voluntary resignation still qualifies
exceptions.desc: Even if you leave for your own reasons, you can receive benefits with a justified reason set by Ministry ordinance (Employment Insurance Act Art. 58, Enforcement Rule Annex 2). Keep evidence such as pay records, medical certificates or complaint records.
items: Unpaid wages: within the year before leaving, all wages or 30% or more unpaid for 2+ months, or pay below minimum wage
Working conditions worse than promised at hiring
The 52-hour weekly limit was exceeded in 2+ months within the year before leaving
Workplace harassment, sexual harassment or sexual assault
Commute of 3+ hours round trip due to office relocation, transfer or moving to live with a spouse
Illness or injury makes work difficult and the company refused leave or reassignment (medical certificate needed)
Leave was refused for family care (30+ days), pregnancy, childbirth or raising a child aged 8 or under
The company's bankruptcy or closure is certain, or mass layoffs are planned
exceptions.link: Calculate benefits with a justified reason

resignationPay.source: Sources: Labor Standards Act Art. 36 and 60, Employee Retirement Benefit Security Act Art. 8 and 9, Employment Insurance Act Art. 40, 45, 46, 48, 50 and 58, National Health Insurance Act Art. 110, Income Tax Act Art. 48, 55 and 59. Estimates based on laws in force as of November 2026.
